scope: Manual de-DE grammar suggestions beyond noun/finite-verb number agreement, from the already qualified native spaCy analysis (de_core_news_sm 3.8.0, CPU/F32) plus pure-Dart planner logic and existing reviewed lexical facts. Native library bytes are unchanged; no new native qualification.

np-agreement.meaning: determiner/adjective agreement with the lexical gender/number of the noun inside one parsed noun phrase (case-independent mismatch, or adjective ending wrong for every compatible determiner/noun reading)

preposition-case.meaning: a noun phrase governed (parse: noun head = preposition, dep nk) by a closed list of fixed-case prepositions whose determiner/adjective/noun are internally consistent but not in the governed case; two-way prepositions never establish a case error

subject-person.meaning: person/number agreement between a parsed subject (dep sb) personal pronoun ich/du/er/wir/ihr/man or common noun and its present-indicative finite verb, using reviewed paradigms only; sie/Sie/es abstain

verb-position.meaning: narrow verb placement: (a) verb-third after one fronted adverbial/prepositional phrase at sentence start, (b) verb-second inside a dass/ob/wenn/obwohl/nachdem/bevor/falls/damit/sobald clause with no other verb or particle; weil-V2 is never flagged

existing_rule: de.spacy.noun-verb (W6/W7) is unchanged and remains enabled in the evaluated configuration; its findings are reported separately and do not count towards any new family.

qualification_panel.authorship: Hand-written by a separate assistant agent from a written brief, without access to the planner implementation or any model output; no external corpus text; no human gold claim.

clean_corpus.source: UD German-GSD r2.15 test split (977 sentences), CC BY-SA 4.0, sentence texts with attribution
clean_corpus.development_counterpart: UD German-GSD r2.15 dev split may be used freely during development (not redistributed here).

development.policy: Implementation uses separate assistant-written development sentences and the GSD dev split only. They never enter a qualification denominator. Initial failures are retained in the record.

configuration_evaluated: SpacyGermanGrammarPlanner with families {noun-verb, np-agreement, preposition-case, subject-person, verb-position} all enabled; request origin 23; same scorer functions as W6 (arm/summarize) applied per family.

arms: deterministic plus native secondary via mergeOfficeProofingReports
scoring.exact_correction: All single-replacement edits applied to the input equal the full expected string; multi-choice findings never count as exact.
scoring.per_family_rows: Error coverage for family F uses the 24 error rows authored for F.
scoring.per_rule_precision: A finding with rule F on ANY valid or guard row (of any family) or on any clean-corpus sentence counts against family F.
scoring.non_exact_native_proposal: A native finding with rule F on an error row whose native-arm output is not exactly the gold.
scoring.recheck: Every combined-exact error output is analyzed and planned again; any remaining native finding is counted.
scoring.parity: Annotations, planner decisions and all arms must be identical case by case on the macOS bundled library and the Linux x86-64 library (only identity.library_sha256 may differ).

predeclared_gate_per_family.clean_corpus: 0 findings, or every finding individually judged a genuine error in the source sentence (judgement recorded with the sentence id)
predeclared_gate_per_family.consequence: A family that fails any gate stays default-off (setting) or is removed; a passing family may be default-on inside the already opt-in manual German grammar provider.

execution_order: Commit and push this protocol, the sealed panel and the clean corpus before running any candidate on them.
Develop on separate data only; record initial failures.
Commit the candidate and write a source seal (sha256 of planner, provider, engine facts and evaluator) before the one-shot run.
Run the qualification exactly once on the macOS bundled library; retain the report whatever the outcome; never rerun or tune against it.
Replay on the Linux x86-64 library on a hosted runner and compare case by case.
Publish the outcome per family; failing families stay default-off.
